title: Realization of restriction-coprojection point transport and its iterates
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, without separatedness [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $A_X=B_X[1/t]$, the sheafification of sectionwise localization. Use ordinary module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,R)$ for the integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $Q_X:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=D^b_c(X,E)$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $F_X:D(B_X)\to D(A_X)$ for $K\mapsto A_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$. Write $J_X(Q_XK)=F_XK$, $J_X(u\otimes a)=aF_X(u)$ for the induced functor. A lisse rational object means an object of the standard heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite sum of coefficient units [def-real-rational-lisse-heart]. A finite locally free module sheaf means one pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_X^{\oplus r}$, allowing rank zero and varying finite ranks.

Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $h:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism. Let $G_h=h^{-1}$ with coefficient action transported by the inverse structural coefficient isomorphism. Let $\sigma_h$ be the integral restriction-and-inverse-image-coprojection map on sections, and $\kappa_{h,C}:G_h^D C\to\widehat P_hC$ the specified completed comparison; define $t_{h,C}=\Gamma(s,\kappa_{h,C})\sigma^D_{h,C}$ as in [def-real-point-automorphism-transport-construction, def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. For every integral $C\in\mathcal C_s$, the scalar-localization comparison of [lem-tw-lisse-point-sections-realization] and the pullback comparison of [lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization] identify $t_{h,C}\otimes_RE$ with the ordinary $A_s$-module-sheaf section transport formed by the same restriction, inverse-image coprojection and module unit.

More precisely, under the specified ordinary-to-completed comparison $\eta_{h,C}$, $\kappa_{h,C}$ becomes the ordinary module unit $z\mapsto1\otimes z$. At every finite quotient its map is reduction followed by that unit and its shifted-product cone coordinate is zero. For a localized section the resulting formula is
$$z/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}\bigl(1\otimes\operatorname{ins}_{h}(\operatorname{res}_{h}z)\bigr).$$
The equality holds for complexes and on derived morphisms, is natural in $C$, commutes with finite coefficient extension, and descends to every lisse rational point object. Under the tensor and pullback composition comparisons specified in [lem-tw-lisse-scalar-comparison-coherence], it also holds for all iterates: the $r$-fold completed transport is identified with the $r$-fold ordinary transport on the successive pulled-back objects, for every integer $r\ge0$, with the zero-fold map the identity. The equality and its iterates respect tensor products and units. No choice of a conjugating fibre isomorphism or field-linearity of $h$ is assumed.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, point automorphism pullback; agent specification of restriction/coprojection normalization and its iterates

proof.text: Write $B=B_s$, $A=A_s$, $G=G_h$, and $P_h^B C=B\otimes^L_{h^{-1}B}h^{-1}C$. The structural map $c_B:h^{-1}B\to B$ is an isomorphism compatible with every residue projection: this is exactly the structure isomorphism in def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, using lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image. Thus the ordinary module pullback is exact and is identified with $G$ by the natural unit $u_C:G C\to P_h^B C$, $z\mapsto1\otimes z$. Indeed its inverse is $b\otimes z\mapsto c_B^{-1}(b)z$; the two composites are the identity by the tensor balancing relation. These are sheaf maps because the formulas commute with restriction and hence sheafify. Both maps commute with differentials. The constructibility theorem lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback ensures $G C$ and $\widehat P_h C$ remain integral constructible, so the sections-localization comparison can subsequently be applied to them. Here $s$ is noetherian of dimension zero and $\ell$ is invertible, and $h$ is an isomorphism, so all these hypotheses hold.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, ordinary pullback along an isomorphism; agent calculation of its unit; Stacks 03D6, sites-modules-definition-pushforward

proof.text: Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to C$ of lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Compute $u$ and the two completed maps on this same resolution. In quotient degree $m$, both $\kappa_{h,P}$ and $\eta_{h,P}u_P$ send $z$ to $1\otimes(z\bmod t^m)$. For the first this is the reduction followed by the unit in part (b) of def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison; for the second it is the stated quotient formula for $\eta$ in lem-tw-ordinary-completed-integral-pullback after applying $u_P$. Their shifted-product coordinates are both zero. Hence these are equal maps to the actual complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, not merely maps with equal individual residue projections. Explicitly, if $\theta_m$ is this common quotient map, then $\theta_m=t_m\theta_{m+1}$, and the cone differential sends $(0,(\theta_m z)_m)$ to $(0,(\theta_m dz)_m)$. Transport along the resolution comparison and the invertible $G(q)$ gives $\kappa_{h,C}=\eta_{h,C}u_C$ in the derived category. Since $\eta_{h,C}$ is invertible for constructible $C$, $\eta_{h,C}^{-1}\kappa_{h,C}=u_C$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 and agent comparison of the specified quotient-cone maps; Stacks 08TC, derived-definition-derived-limit

proof.text: Let $U=(s,\mathrm{id})$, $V=(s,h)$. By lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural, $(G M)(U)=M(V)$ under the specified evaluation comparison, the coprojection at $V$ becomes the identity, and $\sigma_M$ becomes restriction $M(U)\to M(V)$. By lem-tw-lisse-localization-restriction, $F$ is exact sheaf scalar localization with its canonical restriction comparisons. Thus localizing this restriction sends $z/t^n$ to $(z|_V)/t^n$: restriction preserves the constant section $t$. Under evaluation, the inverse-image localization comparison sends this to $\operatorname{ins}_h(\operatorname{res}_h z)/t^n$. This description is compatible with sheafification, since it is first an equality on fractions in the localization presheaf and commutes with restrictions. Under $\lambda_C$ and $\lambda_{GC}$ of lem-tw-lisse-point-sections-realization, this proves that $\sigma_C^D\otimes_R E$ corresponds to the ordinary localized restriction/coprojection map. In particular the comparison is the canonical one, with scalar one. This argument does not identify sections of an arbitrary sheaf tensor product with a tensor product of sections; the required comparison on point sections is precisely the cited $\lambda$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; agent fraction computation using the specified inverse-image evaluation and sections comparisons

proof.text:
By definition $t_{h,C}=\Gamma(s,\kappa_{h,C})\sigma^D_{h,C}$. Substitute step 2, then apply step 3 and the pullback comparison in lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization. The latter uses $F(\eta_{h,C}^{-1})$ and the ordinary scalar-square comparison, which carries the unit to the unit. Consequently the resulting ordinary section map is exactly
$$z/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}\bigl(1\otimes\operatorname{ins}_h(\operatorname{res}_h z)\bigr).$$
The computation in step 2 was on complexes; exact sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms by lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact, and $F$ does so by its exactness in step 3. Thus equality on the chosen resolution gives equality in the derived category. Naturality of $\kappa$ for every derived arrow is supplied by lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-natural; naturality of $\sigma$ is supplied by lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural. Combined with naturality of $\lambda$ and of the pullback comparison, these give naturality of the equality for every integral derived morphism. In the raw rationalization objects are unchanged and arrows are $R$-linear combinations of fractions of integral arrows. Both sides send $v\otimes a$ to $a$ times the integral image, so the equality and its naturality extend to rational arrows. In particular they apply to every lisse rational point object.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 and agent assembly of the specified transport; raw scalar localization as in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, apply lem-weil-point-automorphism-transport-scalar-extension to this very $h$ and $C$, not only to Frobenius. Its rational equation identifies $t_{h,C}\otimes_R E'$ with the scalar extension of $t_{h,C}\otimes_R E$ under the specified point sections and completed pullback comparisons. Lemma lem-tw-lisse-scalar-comparison-coherence identifies their realizations with ordinary coefficient extension, with commuting coefficient squares, localization units, and pullback diagrams. The point-sections maps $\lambda$ are compatible with these comparisons: by lem-tw-lisse-point-sections-realization, $\lambda$ is the termwise map $a\otimes z\mapsto a(1\otimes z)$ and commutes with finite coefficient extension through the specified sections-scalar comparisons. Explicitly, for $z\otimes b\in\Gamma(s,H)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E'}$ the section $\varphi_H^{-1}(z\otimes b)$ is the image of $z\otimes b$ under the sections-tensor map followed by $\chi_H$, and $\lambda_{TH}$ followed by the localized $\chi_H^{-1}$ and the scalar associator of the coherence lemma sends it to $b(1\otimes(1\otimes z))$, which is the coefficient extension of $\lambda_H(z)$. Thus conjugating that equation by the realization maps in step 4 proves finite-extension compatibility of the displayed equality. On fractions the ordinary square has the common value $b\,t^{-n}(1\otimes\operatorname{ins}_h(\operatorname{res}_h z))$ for an additional scalar $b\in E'$. The scalar $t$ here is its image in $E'$, which is invertible even when it is not the chosen uniformizer of $E'$. The cited identity and tower laws ensure the same conclusion for a tower of finite coefficient extensions.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; agent application of the existing normalized point-transport scalar equation

proof.text:
For iteration put $C_0=C$, $C_{j+1}=\widehat P_h C_j$, and $D_0=F_s C$, $D_{j+1}=P_h^A D_j$, where $P_h^A$ is ordinary rational module pullback. Each $C_j$ is constructible by step 1. Write $\nu_C:F_s(\widehat P_h C)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_h^A F_s C$ for the comparison in lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization. Define $\rho_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{j+1}=P_h^A(\rho_j)\nu_{C_j}$, and $e_j=\Gamma(s,\rho_j)\lambda_{C_j}$. If $\tau_D$ denotes ordinary section transport, step 4 at $C_j$, followed by naturality of restriction and the unit for $\rho_j$, gives
$$e_{j+1}(t_{h,C_j}\otimes1)=\tau_{D_j}e_j.$$
Multiplying this equation by the preceding $j$ transport maps proves the assertion for $j+1$ from that for $j$. For $j=0$, $e_0=\lambda_C$ and both empty composites are the identity. This proves every finite iterate, with no use of a formula for a single composite in place of induction. The identity and composition-pullback coherence in lem-tw-lisse-scalar-comparison-coherence identifies the recursively defined $\rho_j$ with the comparisons specified in the statement, independently of parenthesization.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; agent induction on the number of successive pulled-back transports

proof.text: For tensor compatibility, compute before sheafification on local pure tensors. If $T(z)=1\otimes\operatorname{ins}_h(\operatorname{res}_h z)$, restriction and inverse image send $z\otimes w$ to the tensor of their images, and the module unit sends it to $1\otimes(z\otimes w)$. Under the ordinary tensor/pullback associators this is $T(z)\otimes T(w)$. With denominators the common value is $t^{-(a+b)}(T(z)\otimes T(w))$ on $(z/t^a)\otimes(w/t^b)$; on the coefficient unit it is $1\mapsto1$. These formulas are balanced and commute with restrictions, so equality extends from presheaf generators to sheaf tensor products by their defining sheafification property. Use flat-term K-flat representatives for derived tensor, so the same formulas commute with differentials. Lemma lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization identifies the completed tensor and units with exactly these ordinary maps, and lem-tw-lisse-point-sections-realization gives their point normalization. The associativity and unit diagrams of lem-tw-lisse-scalar-comparison-coherence then give tensor and unit compatibility of step 4. Composing these commuting diagrams and using step 6 gives the compatibility for every iterate. On lisse objects these are ordinary module maps in degree zero; rank zero gives the unique maps on zero modules. All computations used $h$ as a scheme automorphism and the specified coefficient maps, with no $k$-linearity or auxiliary fibre conjugation.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Stacks 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product; agent tensor-generator and unit verification

proof_origin.place: Remark 6.8.15 gives the ordinary module pullback, not the specified transport normalization; the proof is the agent chain-level comparison of the existing normalized maps, using Stacks 03D6 and 08TC.
